statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and six representative paths.

page.notes: Public multilingual legal-information MPA. Covered the hub, two legal documents, a technologies index, FAQ, localization, and a failure route. Product account settings, signed-in experiences, downloadable PDFs, archived terms, and external safety/account destinations were not covered because they are separate hosts or authenticated/product flows.

paths.description: Overview/landing template and primary navigation; selected as the entry page and policy hub.
Privacy Policy, representing the longest legal-content template and its in-page reading journey.
Terms of Service, representing dated/versioned legal content and localization.
Technologies listing, representing a section/index template.
Invalid route used to assess HTTP failure and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Page-to-page navigation uses abrupt document swaps rather than view transitions.
findings.evidence: The page probe found no view-transition CSS, while navigation links lead between distinct policy documents.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-origin cross-document View Transitions for policy navigation, with reduced-motion behavior preserved.

findings.summary: Very long policy pages do not expose visible reading progress in the mobile chrome.
findings.evidence: The privacy layout measured 107,024 CSS px of content, while the mobile screenshot shows only a static truncated header and no progress cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress indicator or section-aware header that respects reduced motion.

findings.summary: The mobile header clips or truncates the current-page title.
findings.evidence: At 360px, the Privacy page header renders only “Policy”; Terms renders “Terms of Ser…”. The page probe found no container queries.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the header component adapt to its available inline size with a container query and preserve an unambiguous accessible/visible title.

findings.summary: The 404 state explains the failure but offers no recovery action.
findings.evidence: The invalid route correctly returned HTTP 404, but its screenshot contains no link back to Privacy & Terms, search, or primary navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a branded 404 template with a home/policy-hub link and the normal site navigation.

findings.summary: Mobile lab LCP is above the good Core Web Vitals threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3,906 ms (performance 0.88); a separate desktop trace measured 1,109 ms, so the weakness is condition-dependent rather than universal.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the mobile LCP element and prioritize only its critical font/content dependencies while deferring nonessential scripts.

findings.summary: A parser-inserted high-priority script and font chain compete with initial content.
findings.evidence: The HAR identified a high-priority parser-inserted gstatic script as a render-blocking candidate; three fonts transferred 108,729 bytes and were among the slowest requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Confirm whether the parser script can be deferred, subset/preload only the required font, and avoid loading noncritical font variants before content.

findings.summary: The policy hub ships substantial JavaScript that is unused during initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 248,941 bytes of unused JavaScript and 36,629 bytes of unused CSS. The HAR transferred 503,950 script bytes, including a 159,899-byte tag-manager script.
findings.suggestedFix: Split policy-page code by route and interaction, remove unused OneGoogle modules, and defer analytics/help bundles until needed or consented.

findings.summary: Cache-Control behavior prevents back/forward cache restoration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s BFCache audit failed because the main resource and a JavaScript request used Cache-Control: no-store.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid no-store on public, non-personalized policy documents where possible; isolate personalized state so normal history navigation can use BFCache.

findings.summary: The policy hub has no meta description.
findings.evidence: Both the DOM probe and Lighthouse report no meta[name=description].
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, page-specific meta description explaining the Privacy & Terms hub.

findings.summary: The homepage canonical signal is not accepted as valid by Lighthouse.
findings.evidence: The DOM exposes canonical https://policies.google.com/?hl=en-US, but Lighthouse’s canonical audit fails for the requested https://policies.google.com/ URL. robots.txt and sitemap.xml also returned 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Align canonical and locale URLs consistently, expose hreflang alternatives, and publish discoverable robots/sitemap endpoints for the multilingual policy corpus.

findings.summary: The public policy hub has no Open Graph or structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The page probe found zero Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph metadata and appropriate Organization/WebPage JSON-LD that matches the visible page.

findings.summary: A privacy-policy hub loads analytics and seven third-party origins on first view.
findings.evidence: The tracker capture found Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics among seven third-party origins; the HAR shows the tag-manager script alone transferred 159,899 bytes. No sensitive secret was found; detected Google API keys are public client configuration.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove analytics from policy pages where possible, or gate and minimize it; load help/account integrations only after explicit use.

findings.summary: Several defensive response policies are absent or permissive.
findings.evidence: The headers capture found no HSTS header, no Referrer-Policy, and neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors. CSP uses nonces and Trusted Types, but one policy still advertises unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline allowances.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit HSTS and Referrer-Policy, add frame-ancestors unless embedding is intentional, and remove obsolete unsafe allowances after validating the effective multi-policy CSP.

findings.summary: Small decorative images omit intrinsic dimensions and below-fold lazy loading.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all six images without width/height attributes and two below-fold images without loading=lazy; observed CLS remained 0 and no image was oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare intrinsic width/height and lazy-load below-fold decorative images; retain empty alt or presentational semantics for decoration.
